answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust with bounded-length random walks, choosing edges by weight. A sybil cluster behind a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walks from honest seeds enter it. Its reachable trust—and thus delegated voting weight—is bounded by cut capacity relative to cluster volume and seed mass, preventing internal endorsements from compounding without outside support. An onyx cluster cannot become a lantern merely by balancing on a ledge of mutual attestations.
